title: Certificates Among Enumerated Ranks
statement: Let $V\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ be a language, and let $x$ be a binary word and $w\in\mathbb{N}$. Testing the $2^w$ consecutive ranks starting at zero, accepting rank $i$ exactly when $x$ concatenated with the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ belongs to $V$, returns true if and only if there is a binary word $u$ of length $w$ such that $x$ concatenated with $u$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language over the binary alphabet
replaced:
Let $V$ be a language over the binary alphabet, $x$ a string, and $w$ a width.
Testing all $2^w$ ranks with the acceptance function ``the indicator of $V$ accepts
$x$ concatenated with the width-$w$ binary word of the rank'' returns true if and
only if there exists $u$ with $|u| = w$ and $x \mathbin{+\!\!+} u \in V$.
